title: gammaln
summary: Compute the natural logarithm of the gamma function element-wise in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Uses the provider unary_gammaln hook after proving real GPU inputs are nonnegative; falls back to host evaluation when the hook is unavailable.

description: `Y = gammaln(A)` evaluates `log(gamma(A))` for real nonnegative inputs while avoiding the overflow that can occur when computing `gamma(A)` first.
behaviors: `gammaln(A)` applies the log-gamma function element-by-element while preserving the input tensor shape.
Double inputs return double results; single tensors preserve single dtype metadata with single-rounded output values.
Scalar integer, logical, and character inputs are promoted through RunMat's ordinary numeric coercion path for compatibility with existing elementwise builtins.
Negative, complex, string, and sparse inputs produce stable typed errors.
Real GPU tensors stay on device when the provider implements `unary_gammaln`; otherwise RunMat gathers the tensor, evaluates on the host, and returns a host value with the computed results.

examples.description: Evaluate the log-gamma function at a scalar
Apply gammaln element-wise to an array
Avoid gamma overflow for large inputs

faqs.question: Why use `gammaln(A)` instead of `log(gamma(A))`?
faqs.answer: `gammaln` evaluates the logarithm directly, so large positive inputs can remain finite even when `gamma(A)` would overflow before the logarithm is taken.

faqs.question: Does `gammaln` support complex or negative inputs?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB documents `gammaln` for real nonnegative input, and RunMat reports typed errors for complex and negative values.

faqs.question: Can `gammaln` run on GPU arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes for real nonnegative tensors. The WGPU backend evaluates `gammaln` on device; other providers may fall back to host evaluation if they do not expose `unary_gammaln`.

gpu_residency: Yes when the active provider implements `unary_gammaln` for real-valued gpuArray inputs. Providers without that hook trigger a host fallback, so the computed result is returned as a host tensor rather than a resident gpuArray.
implementation_notes: CPU evaluation uses a log-Lanczos approximation and the reflection identity for positive inputs below 0.5.
The WGPU backend uses the same log-Lanczos form for f32 and f64 precision.
RunMat validates the real nonnegative domain before executing provider kernels so negative inputs produce stable domain errors.
